findings.title: CRLF-completed output loses visible line bodies during progress folding
findings.cause: split("\n") leaves CR at the end of each CRLF segment. lastIndexOf("\r") then points to that last character, so slice(lastCr+1) replaces the completed visible line with an empty segment.
findings.ordinaryTrigger: A short background stdout/stderr slice containing a completed CRLF line, such as ready\r\n. The real onData/ring/readOutput/BashOutput chain accepts and forwards such raw text without prior newline normalization in the statically read source.
findings.contract: The leaf and BashOutput promise cleaned process output with ANSI/progress noise removed; ordinary completed line text and the final progress frame remain meaningful output. Literal LF expectations test visible text preservation, not byte-exact CRLF serialization.
findings.actualValidation: Actual output-clean leaf imported directly, four current-wrong-result characterizations and two controls plus seven existing tests in one guarded first shard: 13 pass/23 expect/0 fail/0 skipped/Completed/exit0. Passing characterizations are not a fix.
findings.impact: The agent-facing BashOutput body loses ordinary CRLF line text in either read mode when that complete line is present in the cleaned slice. A newline remains, so the tool usually returns blank lines; (no new output) is not guaranteed. Incremental raw offset advancement occurs before cleaning in static source, not a dynamically verified manager result.
counterevidence: LF text and intentional bare-CR progress folding retain expected behavior in the focused controls.
Only short ASCII strings are characterized; no cap, wraparound, UTF-8, ANSI parser or chunk-boundary expansion.
Ring data is retained as raw Buffer and disk mirror is best effort; cleanup does not rewrite the raw ring/disk. This is not disk corruption or an assertion that disk persistence always succeeds.
No Windows, PTY, shell, manager, tool, session, model or actual filesystem workflow was executed; consumer reachability is source-only.
findings.novelty: All recursive docs/bugs MD and JSON scalar history searched excluding round25. Selected exact output-clean mentions were contracts/inventories; old frontmatter, patch, simplediff, NDJSON, pagination and ANSI mechanisms differ and were not reopened. Keyword search is not semantic exhaustion.
